correctness.rationale: An explicit distance table proves every minimum ordinary vertex-metric basis has exactly one empty matched pair and one chosen endpoint at every other pair. All legal basis-preserving slides are precisely vacancy transfers with a side flip. The proof inducts from C12, fixing shared endpoints or using two fully specified vacancy itineraries. The sharp lower bound counts a->b versus b->a slides and forces at least two reverse slides when the vacancy is restored, yielding exactly n+3 for every n>=3. The direct checker exhaustively reconstructs bases from original graph distances for n=3..7; a separate state checker verifies all-pairs diameters n=3..8 and explicit constructive routes through n=11. These tests corroborate the proof, not replace it.

value.rationale: The diameter is the natural worst-case number of adjacency-constrained relocations of a minimum set of distance sensors while preserving optimal distinguishability at every intermediate state. The n+3 formula is exact and sharp throughout an infinite graph family, rather than a numerical small-case observation or re-expression of the already-known basis count. Explicit route constructions establish the mobility guarantee, while the two unavoidable reverse slides explain the nontrivial additive four-step penalty above the n−1 side flips.
